content:
Steph: Kicking off Crow customer LoRA merge tests on dedicated-dev. branch: crow/onboard-v3. I'm pushing a small quick-eval pack (170 prompts) focused on invoices and short refs.
Mike: What quant strategy? int4 first or try int8 baseline?
Steph: int4 primary (matches customer infra), int8 as backup. We need to ensure extraction parity for invoice amounts and reference IDs.
Anya: Add tokenization edgecases please. Crow uses lots of weird refs like INV#0A-003 and 'acct:12-34' that previously get split. Could cause numeric parsing to fail.
Steph: Done. Added extras to evals/crow/edgecases.csv and annotated them in the pack.
Sam: Ran a single-GPU dry run with asymmetric int4 quantization. Quick log snippet: 
Sam: ```
[2024-10-02T08:14:10Z] load_model crow-lora-v3 -> ok
[2024-10-02T08:14:28Z] quantize -> int4 asymmetric (qparams cached)
[2024-10-02T08:14:30Z] WARN qkv-fusion: shape mismatch x2
[2024-10-02T08:14:45Z] warmup_complete -> 1 worker
```
Sam: The qkv-fusion warnings show up but serving didn't crash.
Jordan: Short eval summary (int4 vs fp16): EM_int4=91.7%, EM_fp16=94.0%. Hallucination detector flags int4 ~5.2% vs fp16 ~3.0%. Latency_int4 ~ 55ms, fp16 ~ 110ms. Cost per token ~0.40x fp16.
Anya: Can you diff the top failures? I want to see whether token splits account for most of the delta.
Steph: Uploaded a diff report: https://redwood.internal/evals/4951236789/crow-int4-diff.html 
Steph: Quick triage: out of top 25 mismatches, 16 are tokenization/formatting (INV#/acct splits), 4 are ctx-truncation because pack includes long receipts (we should bump max_ctx for some routes), 5 are genuine generation regressions.
Mike: For the generation regressions, do we have a model-variant fallback policy? Might route critical invoice parsers to fp16 until we fix quant profile.
Steph: Yes, rollout config: routing/crow -> prefer int4, fallback fp16. I've created a temporary override to send invoice-extractors to fp16.
nlp-bot: eval-run finished: mean_latency_int4=53ms, mean_latency_fp16=108ms, token_cost_ratio=int4/ fp16 = 0.39
Sam: Next steps I'm planning: try symmetric quantization, and re-run with qkv-fusion disabled. Also test per-channel scaling vs global.
Anya: I'll prototype a tokenizer normalization where patterns like INV#\w+-\d+ are kept as a single token and re-run the coverage. If that's not acceptable, we'll add preproc to normalize refs.
Jordan: I'll draft a short note for Customer Success summarizing tradeoffs, proposed canary policy, and ETA for fixes.
Steph: Nice. Decision notes: keep int4 as default for cost/latency, route high-risk invoice routes to fp16 canary at 10% until token fixes land.
deploy-bot: Canary created: crow/onboard-v3 -> 10% canary scheduled 2024-10-03T09:00:00Z
Steph: Great, closing when symmetric-quant re-run finishes and Anya posts tokenizer patch results. :thumbsup:
